scenes.heading: Parallel and perpendicular lines
scenes.sub: Gradients tell you if lines never meet or cross square
scenes.say: Railway tracks never meet. A crossroads makes a perfect square corner. On a graph, the gradients tell you which is which.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Railway tracks never meet; a crossroads meets square
scenes.science: Parallel: same gradient. Perpendicular: gradients multiply to −1
scenes.breaks: Real tracks curve and roads are wide; lines are perfectly straight with no width.
scenes.say: Two railway tracks run at exactly the same slope, so they never meet. That's parallel. A neat crossroads meets at a square corner. That's perpendicular. Lines on a graph are perfectly straight and have no width, so we can test them exactly.

scenes.heading: Parallel: same gradient
scenes.say: Here are y equals half x plus two, and y equals half x minus one. First one line, then the other. Both have gradient one half, so they climb at the same rate and the gap between them never closes.
scenes.caption: y = ½x + 2 and y = ½x − 1: same gradient ½, so they are parallel.

scenes.heading: Perpendicular gradients
scenes.say: For perpendicular lines, the gradients multiply to negative one. So flip the fraction and switch the sign. The negative reciprocal of two is negative one half. Of two thirds, it's negative three halves.
scenes.caption: m₁ × m₂ = −1. Flip and switch: 2 → −½, ⅔ → −3/2.

scenes.heading: Perpendicular: a square corner
scenes.say: Now y equals two x minus one, then y equals negative half x plus four. They cross at two, three, and the little square marks the right angle. Check: two times negative one half is negative one.
scenes.caption: y = 2x − 1 and y = −½x + 4 cross at (2, 3). 2 × (−½) = −1.

scenes.heading: Perpendicular line through a point
scenes.question: Find the line perpendicular to y = 2x − 1 through (2, 3).
scenes.say: Find the line perpendicular to y equals two x minus one, through two, three. The new gradient is negative one half. Substitute the point: three equals negative one plus c, so c is four. The line is y equals negative half x plus four.
scenes.caption: m = −½. 3 = −½(2) + c, so c = 4: y = −½x + 4.

scenes.heading: Parallel or perpendicular?
scenes.say: Parallel lines share the same gradient and never meet. Perpendicular lines have gradients that multiply to negative one and meet at ninety degrees. And always rearrange to y equals m x plus c before you compare.

points: Flip the fraction, switch the sign
Then substitute a point for c
scenes.say: Recap. Parallel lines have equal gradients. Perpendicular gradients multiply to negative one: flip and switch. Rearrange first, then substitute a point to find c. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Parallel: equal gradients. Perpendicular: m₁ × m₂ = −1. Rearrange first, then substitute a point for c. Now try the practice questions!
